mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registered Matters (Company Registration Extract / Certificate of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office, Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certificate issued by the Korean court registry, then certified by a notary public or court confirmation, followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille affixed under the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular legalization applies only for a destination that is not an Apostille Convention state; the two authentication methods are parallel alternatives and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Existence and No Dissolution Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office and National Tax Service Business Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For non-member states, use the separate consular legalization route of notarization, court or prosecution confirmation, MOFA legalization, and destination embassy authentication; do not chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Execution of Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa Board of Directors, certified by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the board resolution and power of attorney before a Korean notary public, then obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For non-member jurisdictions, the parallel path is notarization, MOFA legalization, then consular legalization at the destination embassy; never use both systems for the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa and the Local District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified copy of the Articles of Association, notarized if required, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization is the mutually exclusive alternative only when the receiving jurisdiction is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Chusik Hoesa Corporate Account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Bank maintaining the corporate settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank-issued letter under corporate seal, certified by a notary public, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Consular legalization remains a separate parallel route for non-Apostille destinations and must not be added after an Apostille has already been issued.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be completed before formation and repeated every 30 days while the corporate relationship remains active. The compliance program must verify each director, shareholder, UBO, signatory, client, and counterparty against OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Korean government domestic sanctions designations. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons must be identified through reliable electronic databases, corroborated by corporate registries and available public records, and require senior management approval before onboarding. Beneficial ownership must be traced through each corporate layer to natural persons holding at least 25 percent of shares or control. Although the marine cargo surveyor business is categorized as Low_Risk_Standard, the use of underwriter wires and Wise transfers requires enhanced due diligence on unusual payment flows. All screening results, source documentation, and negative news hits must be retained for at least five years after account closure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registration Information Network (IROS / Internet Registration Office)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa must adopt a business name registrable in Korean script under the Commercial Act. The name must contain the statutory corporate suffix meaning Chusik Hoesa in Korean and must follow the four-tier naming structure: distinctive element, business purpose phrase, corporate form indicator, and optional jurisdictional or auxiliary transliteration. Foreign names in Latin script may be used as an auxiliary transliteration alongside the Korean statutory name. Phonetic conversion from English to Hangul must follow official Korean transliteration rules. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name in the same court district and must not imply a regulated industry the entity is not legally licensed to conduct.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must within the time limit stated in the rejection notice, typically 14 days, file a written administrative objection with the competent district court registration office. The objection must include the representative's signature, the corrected proposed name, a comparison of conflicting registrations, and the statutory filing fee. If the initial objection is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent administrative court within 90 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal should assert legal error, inadequate review, or abuse of discretion by the registrar. Legal counsel should be engaged to ensure compliance with procedural deadlines and to present the distinctive element of the proposed name clearly.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Chusik Hoesa carrying on marine cargo surveying, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable without a genuine physical office in Korea. The Commercial Act and the National Tax Service require an actual head office address for service of process, tax registration, and corporate bookkeeping. Korean banks reject corporate account applications supported only by virtual addresses and require a lease agreement, utility records, and either an on-site visit or notarized confirmation. Coworking suites may be accepted if they provide a physical desk, signage rights, mail handling, and immediate access to records and responsible personnel. The entity must be able to demonstrate commercial substance over form at the registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is estimated at 30 to 40 percent during the first 18 months, driven by National Tax Service field inspections on VAT refunds and registry verification of address irregularities. Inspection readiness checklist: physical lease agreement in the company name; office signage displaying the Korean company name; actual furniture, computer equipment, and corporate records; authorized employee or director present during business hours; corporate registration extract available; corporate seal and bank documents; board minutes and accounting books; and evidence of active marine surveying such as contracts, survey reports, and insurance credentials.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288-370 (Stock Corporation), and the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 1029, as amended)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry (등기소) under the Supreme Court of Korea, specifically the local district court registry with jurisdiction over the company's registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Application for Registration of Incorporation (설립등기신청서)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all issued shares must be fully paid in at incorporation, and the capital must be deposited in a bank account in the name of the company or the incorporator before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA)

Pursuant to the Commercial Act of South Korea and the Articles of Incorporation of [Company Name] (the 'Company'), the first meeting of the Board of Directors was duly convened and held on [date] at [time] at the registered office of the Company. All directors were present, and the meeting was conducted in accordance with the law and the Articles of Incorporation.

The following resolutions were unanimously adopted:

1. Subscription and Allotment of Shares: The Board of Directors ratifies the subscription and allotment of the Company's shares as set forth in the subscription agreements. The Board confirms that the total issued shares have been fully subscribed and paid in by the initial shareholders, and that the paid-in capital of [amount] Korean Won has been deposited in the Company's capital deposit account at [Bank Name] as required by law.

2. Adoption of Registered Office: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [address], which shall be the principal place of business and the legal seat of the Company. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to execute any lease or purchase agreements and to file all necessary registrations with the competent Court Registry.

3. Appointment of Statutory Officers: The Board appoints the following officers: [Name] as Representative Director (CEO), [Name] as Director, and [Name] as Auditor (if required). The officers shall have the powers and duties as prescribed by law and the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director is hereby authorized to represent the Company in all transactions and to execute all documents on behalf of the Company.

4. Banking Authorization: The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and designates the Representative Director and [Name] as authorized signatories. The Board further authorizes the execution of any banking agreements and the use of the corporate seal as required.

5. Corporate Seal and Documentation: The Board approves the adoption of the Company's corporate seal and the use of the Company's name and seal on all official documents. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to arrange for the notarization of the seal and to file the necessary documents with the relevant authorities.

6. General Authorization: The Board authorizes the Representative Director and any other officers to take all necessary actions, execute all documents, and complete all filings required to complete the incorporation and registration of the Company, including but not limited to registration with the Court Registry, the tax office, and any other regulatory bodies.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

[Signature of Chairman] [Date]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and local Court Registry (등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, business purpose, registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the number of directors and auditors. The Articles must be notarized by a notary public to confirm the legality and authenticity. After notarization, the incorporators must subscribe to the shares and pay the full capital into a temporary bank account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit, which is a prerequisite for registration. Ensure all incorporators provide valid identification and proof of address.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Bank certificate of capital deposit (to be obtained after payment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the Articles and resubmit. If the bank delays the certificate, follow up with the bank and provide additional identification if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Obtaining Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the incorporator or the company (pre-incorporation) and deposit the full amount of paid-in capital. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit confirming the amount and the account holder. This certificate is mandatory for the incorporation registration. Ensure the deposit is made in Korean Won and that the bank's stamp and signature are affixed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, provide additional identification or clarify the purpose. If the certificate is delayed, request an expedited issuance or obtain a provisional certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for incorporation registration to the court registry with jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of deposit, the list of directors and auditor, and the seal registration form. Pay the registration fee (approximately 300 USD) and submit all documents. The registry will review the application and, if satisfied, issue a certificate of incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: List of directors and auditor with consent forms
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, respond within the specified period (usually 2 weeks) with corrected documents or additional explanations. If the application is rejected, rectify the issues and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) - local district office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the certificate of incorporation registration, file for business registration (사업자등록) with the local tax office. Provide the certificate of incorporation, lease agreement for the registered office, and the company's corporate seal. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate, which is required for tax purposes and for opening a corporate bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the application, correct any discrepancies in the address or company details and reapply. If additional documents are requested, provide them promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) - Marine Safety Division

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable as the business is a professional service with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing operations. No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office premises is required under the Fire Services Act (소방시설법). The office must pass a fire safety inspection and obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire department. Occupational safety clearance is required from the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) for workplace safety compliance, including emergency evacuation plans and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea – online electronic portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) – UNI-PASS electronic clearance system for export and customs formalities
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident contributor forming a Chusik Hoesa must ensure the Korean company obtains a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the single tax identity for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and electronic tax invoicing. The statutory procedure is: (1) complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act and remit paid-in capital through a Korean bank; (2) within 20 days of commencing business, file the national business registration application with the competent NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean place of business, or through HomeTax where a tax representative is appointed; (3) attach the certified articles of incorporation, apostilled/consularized foreign certificate of incorporation or corporate good-standing certificate, board resolution approving the Korean entity and tax representative appointment, power of attorney naming a Korean tax representative if the non-resident has no Korean permanent establishment, proof of registered office address, and identity documents of the statutory representative; (4) obtain the NTS-issued 10-digit BRN after validation. There is no separate VAT registration number: the BRN is concurrently the VAT Taxpayer Reference Number and the Corporate Taxpayer Reference Number. A foreign entity with no domestic place of business but with VAT obligations in Korea must appoint a tax representative and register the same BRN procedure for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean tax system does not provide a check-the-box, hybrid mismatch, or pass-through classification election for a Chusik Hoesa; the entity is per se taxable as a domestic corporation on worldwide income. A parent resident corporation holding at least 90% of a resident subsidiary may elect consolidated corporate income tax filing for qualifying wholly-owned domestic subsidiary groups, and a corporation may, with NTS approval, use a fiscal year other than the calendar year; these are filing and accounting-period elections, not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW turnover threshold for a Chusik Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory within 20 days of business commencement regardless of revenue level. The KRW 80,000,000 annual revenue threshold is relevant only for simplified taxable person status (small business VAT simplification), not as a registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (ETI) must be issued through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system for all VAT taxable supplies, including B2B supplies; transmission to the NTS must occur by the following business day after issuance. Commercial accounting systems connect through the NTS Open API. There is no pre-issuance real-time fiscal clearance or physical/crypto anti-fraud stamping requirement comparable to Latin American fiscal voucher regimes; instead, the NTS performs near-real-time validation of invoice metadata (BRN, supply value, VAT amount, line-item descriptions), cross-references ETI records against Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign-exchange bank receipts, and applies anti-fraud risk scoring to flag abnormal or missing documentation. Export invoices must carry the 0% VAT category code and identify the supporting export document reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act and the Presidential Decree applies only to: (i) goods physically exported from the Korean customs territory, supported by an accepted KCS Customs Export Declaration; (ii) services supplied and consumed/used wholly outside Korea; and (iii) services specifically designated as foreign currency earning services (e.g., certain international trade and export-related services listed in the Presidential Decree) that are provided to a non-resident foreign insurer and paid in convertible foreign currency. For a marine insurance surveyor inspecting vessel hulls or cargo damage in Korea, 0% VAT cannot be assumed merely because the insurer is a foreign underwriter; the service must satisfy the statutory place-of-supply test or fall within a designated foreign-currency-earning category. Qualifying exported digital content or offshore services also require that the recipient is outside Korea and that the supply is not consumed in Korea. Payment must be received in foreign exchange and repatriated into Korea through a domestic foreign exchange bank.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) – Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export clearance record
Bill of Lading (or air waybill for air cargo) evidencing physical departure of goods from the Korean customs territory to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt and repatriation of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS conducts post-export audits by matching electronic tax invoices against UNI-PASS customs declarations and FIRCs. If the 0% rate is unsupported, omitted, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the zero-rating is revoked and the taxpayer is assessed the unpaid 10% VAT plus refund clawbacks with interest. Administrative penalty taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes follow: 10% for underreported tax bases, 20% for false reporting, and 40% for deliberate concealment, along with delay penalties for overdue VAT. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act may be initiated for forged export documents, fabricated FIRCs, or intentional VAT refund fraud, and the taxpayer may lose eligibility for future zero-rated export treatment and be excluded from NTS compliance-good-benefit programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Administration; day-to-day compliance reporting is channelled through authorized foreign exchange banks and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, South Korea maintains a semi-liberalised regime: current account payments are generally convertible and freely remittable when supported by an underlying trade or service contract. Cross-border service receipts from marine insurance surveying, cargo inspection, and claims adjudication are treated as current account earnings and may be settled through an authorized foreign exchange bank without prior approval, provided the bank receives the invoice, service confirmation, and related evidence for purpose code classification. Capital account transactions, however, require structured reporting and in some cases prior declaration or approval. Foreign direct investment into a Korean Chusik Hoesa must be registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the invested capital recorded after remittance and verification by the receiving bank. Dividend repatriation is permitted for registered foreign-invested companies after local corporate tax settlement, audited financial statements, and bank confirmation of distributable reserves, with applicable withholding tax and any double tax treaty relief applied. The Korean won is not freely tradable offshore; onshore deliverable liquidity is restricted, and offshore non-deliverable won instruments require genuine underlying exposure. There is no general mandatory conversion of service export proceeds in Korea, but companies must collect export/survey earnings within the statutory settlement timeline and report all movements through the banking system. Profits can be remitted once the foreign investment entity registration is valid and the tax clearance obligations are met.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For marine insurance surveying services exported by a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the service provider must receive the foreign-currency settlement within six months from the date the survey report is issued. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; export proceeds may be retained in a foreign currency deposit account at an authorized foreign exchange bank. The bank must receive a copy of the survey contract, the invoice, the proof of performance, and the payment instruction. If payment is not received within the statutory six-month period, the exporter must submit an extension application to the foreign exchange bank explaining the commercial dispute or bank delay. Delayed receipts require a retroactive foreign exchange declaration and risk administrative fines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under Korean foreign exchange legislation, only an authorized foreign exchange bank may hold and settle corporate Korean won treasury operations for a domestic Chusik Hoesa. Wise and other unlicensed international EMIs are not authorized foreign exchange banks and are legally barred from serving as the primary clearing or operating account provider for a Korean resident corporate entity. The entity may use an EMI only as an ancillary outbound disbursement channel for very low-value payments to foreign beneficiaries outside Korea, and even then the Korean bank may require the underlying invoices to be disclosed. The statutory treasury blueprint must be anchored on a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank; the EMI rail cannot support capital verification, VAT refund processes, foreign exchange reporting, or dividend outbound remittances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one statutory director at the selected Korean Tier-1 bank branch is required as the baseline corporate onboarding procedure. A remote consular proxy opening is possible only in exceptional scenarios where the foreign parent is a regulated financial institution and the Korean bank accepts an apostilled power of attorney, a notarized UBO identity dossier, and a live international video interview with the non-resident director. Even in that exception, a resident Korea-based signatory or a company secretary who can receive the e-certificate, Hong Kong-style device token, and respond to transaction monitoring calls is practically necessary. For a marine insurance surveying entity with foreign underwriters, the bank AML committee will likely insist on an in-person or video-interviewed executive to explain the survey fee flow, the professional licensing, and the sanctions-screening process. The fastest and most reliable path is a physical director visit to Seoul or Busan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain includes foreign insurance pools, captives, and holding entities with fragmented disclosure and no obvious physical operating profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a transparent ownership chart; notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation for every entity in the chain; audited financial statements for the ultimate parent; scanned passports and proof of residential address for each natural-person UBO; a board resolution from the foreign shareholder approving the Korean investment; and a sworn source-of-wealth statement from the ultimate beneficial owner explaining the origin of the Korean capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory marine surveyor licensing and professional indemnity coverage are not clearly evidenced at account onboarding, creating a regulatory mismatch between the stated business scope and the claimed service revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Chusik Hoesa corporate register extract showing the authorised clause for vessel hull and cargo damage survey, marine claims inspection, and loss adjustment; the applicable Korean insurance surveyor licence or professional registration; a valid professional indemnity insurance policy; English-language specimen survey reports; and a letter of engagement from an admitted marine underwriter appointing the company as an approved surveyor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows from high-risk offshore jurisdictions and non-bank claims offices may resemble money transmission or unlicensed insurance activity if the transaction purpose codes are vague.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a detailed transaction flow memorandum for each foreign underwriter; provide the underwriter's regulated status in its home jurisdiction; include sanctions and PEP screening reports on all counterparties; include IMO vessel registration evidence for inspected hulls; produce signed marine survey contracts, detailed invoices, and bank references for the payer; and submit a compliance officer attestation that no premium collection, underwriting, or policy selling is performed by the Korean entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming shareholder funding is structured as a convertible loan or mixed-purpose remittance, which confuses the foreign investment capital verification and foreign exchange reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Use the Foreign Investment Promotion Act equity injection route for all capital contributions; provide the foreign investment report receipt number; ensure the SWIFT remittance reference contains the registered investor identifier and the precise purpose code; if convertible loan funding is unavoidable, submit the loan agreement, Bank of Korea foreign currency borrowing declaration number, confirmation that interest is at arm's length, and a commitment from the shareholders to convert only after bank and MOEF approval. A Korean certified public accountant must issue the capital verification report after the funds are credited.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be wired to a designated foreign exchange bank account in the name of the Korean Chusik Hoesa using SWIFT MT103 or MT202. The remitter must be exactly the foreign investor of record under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the payment narrative must contain the foreign investment report number, the investor identifier, and the purpose code for foreign direct investment. After receipt, the bank issues a certificate of foreign currency payment, the company completes capital verification with an external Korean CPA, and the registration of the foreign-invested company is updated with the MOEF and relevant tax authority. For operational service inflows, payments from marine underwriters should be denominated in USD or another convertible currency and coded as service export earnings, supported by the survey contract, invoice, and bank arrival notice. All transactions must be reported by the bank through the Foreign Exchange Information Network and must be traceable to the underlying commercial purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade, surveyor fee, subcontractor, reinsurance premium, and claims-related disbursements is SWIFT MT103 through the Korean foreign exchange bank. The Korean bank will create a foreign exchange settlement report and assign a purpose code based on the invoice, the beneficiary country, and the nature of the payment. For high-value or documentary transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit or Standby Letter of Credit can be issued in favour of a foreign sub-surveyor or equipment supplier when the recipient requires banking payment confirmation. Documentary Collections may be used only where the transport and waiver documents are needed before payment release, which is rare in a marine survey fee context. The company must maintain a disbursement ledger showing the underlying contract, bank beneficiary, and purpose code for every outward wire to ensure full FIEINET and tax reporting conformity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Korean won versus US dollar FX forwards with a maximum tenor of twelve months, permitted only to hedge confirmed marine survey receivables from foreign underwriters; the bank requires an invoice schedule and proof of the underlying service contract.

Non-deliverable forwards in USD/KRW for offshore counterparty exposure, permitted only when the hedge is linked to a real cross-border trade or investment transaction and the underlying exposure does not require onshore won settlement; no speculative NDF trading is allowed.

Currency swaps or rolling swaps between KRW and foreign currencies for long-term hull surveying equipment leases and capital disbursements, subject to prior foreign exchange bank approval, FIEINET registration, and documented commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and financial statements, including approved balance sheet and profit and loss statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea through the Hometax electronic portal; administered by the District Tax Office having local jurisdiction over the company's principal place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, the filing is due by March 31 of the following year, with tax return extension provisions available under the Framework Act for National Taxes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting corporate income tax attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unfiled or underreported corporate tax (40% for a false return or fraudulent tax avoidance), plus an overdue interest surcharge calculated at the statutory monthly rate of approximately 0.6% until the unpaid tax is settled. Continuous delinquency can trigger personal director liability, seizure of corporate assets, cancellation of business registration and enforced closure by the tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders (annual general meeting) for approval of the audited or unaudited financial statements and a dividend resolution, with signed minutes placed in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa; the minutes are retained at the registered office and certified by the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular shareholders' meeting must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (by March 31 for a calendar-year company); if the meeting is not held, shareholder remedial procedures including judicial request to convene a shareholders' meeting are available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the annual meeting within the statutory period are in breach of the Korean Commercial Act and may be subject to damages claims and administrative penalties; profits distributed without valid ordinary-shareholder approval may be voidable, and the company's financial statements become defective for tax filing, exposing the company to tax and audit penalty surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA audit report and audited financial statements, if the company is at or above the mandatory external audit threshold; copy delivered to the Financial Supervisory Service and attached to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of South Korea; National Tax Service (NTS) for the return attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must deliver the audit report in time for the regular shareholders' meeting; the audited financial statements must be attached to the corporate income tax return, filing by March 31 for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a mandatory-audit company fails to appoint an auditor or file the audit report, the Financial Supervisory Service may designate an auditor automatically, impose administrative fines, and refer the matter for penal sanction; the tax return will be treated as incomplete, causing unfaithful tax return penalties and 0.6% monthly overdue interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration amendments for director, auditor, registered office, authorised capital and encumbrance changes arising from the annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered address in South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks (14 days) from the date of the relevant resolution, including AGM resolutions reappointing or replacing directors or auditors; nil filing if no registered item changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted registration of a director or auditor change is a violation of the Korean Commercial Act exposing the company and responsible officers to administrative fines, obstructions to third-party reliance on the registry, and judicial strike-off or deemed-dissolution procedures for a persistently non-compliant dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Alteration Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, filed only where the Chusik Hoesa is a foreign-invested company and a share transfer or equity change occurs; used also to confirm ultimate beneficial ownership status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) of South Korea through KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the shareholding transfer or registered equity change; no separate annual UBO report exists under Korean corporate law.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within 30 days can result in cancellation of foreign-invested-enterprise recognition, loss of foreign investment protection and tax incentives, and an administrative fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; recurrent failure may block a foreign investor's participation in capital transactions and dividend repatriation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa is subject to a compulsory independent audit by a certified CPA if any of the following applies: (a) it is a listed company (KOSPI, KOSDAQ or KONEX) irrespective of asset size; (b) it is an unlisted company whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.7 million at the KRW/USD exchange rate used for the compliance cycle); (c) it is a supervised financial company, insurance company, securities company or other special-law company, regardless of asset size; or (d) it is licensed as an insurance claims adjuster or marine surveyor under the Korean Insurance Business Act and designated by supervisory regulations as subject to external audit. These tests are balance-sheet-based; the Korean External Audit Act does not use turnover or headcount as audit triggers for private unlisted corporations. A company below the threshold is not legally required to appoint an external CPA auditor, but such an audit may be voluntarily adopted by shareholder resolution or required under a foreign parent group governance policy.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: From incorporation, a Chusik Hoesa prepares financial statements under the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if it is listed or subject to the external audit mandate; a non-listed company below the audit threshold may apply the Korean General Accounting Standards for Non-Public Entities (Korean GAAP/K-GAAP). Consolidated and separate financial statements prepared for statutory reporting must be expressed in KRW and follow the hierarchy of the Korean Accounting Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a publicly searchable annual UBO return for ordinary Chusik Hoesa. Instead, the board and corporate secretary must internally confirm, at least once per year and no later than the annual general meeting, the identity and economic ownership of every registered shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner of 25% or more of shares or voting rights, updating the Korean AML/KYC records used with banks and counterparties. Any share transfer, including a transfer to or from a non-resident, must be reflected in the company shareholder register and, if the company is a foreign-invested enterprise, reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of the transfer. Domestic non-resident share transfers do not create a central UBO filing obligation; the record to keep is the shareholder register and foreign investment alteration report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,200 per year for a registered Korean office and qualified company secretarial agent in Seoul or Busan.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a mandatory certified CPA audit of a private marine insurance surveyor above the threshold; 0 if no statutory audit is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax plus 10% local surtax (total 27.5% marginal rate; progressive rates 10-25%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small/medium enterprise (SME) reduced rates and R&D tax credit under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; no general patent-box regime; special tax support available for qualified foreign-invested technology ventures; Korean-source income of a foreign corporation without a permanent establishment is subject to final withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세 과세표준 세액신고서) using National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing system; for foreign-owned corporations, Form 22-3 / attached schedules A, B, C as needed
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., March 31 for December 31 year-end); one-month extension allowed upon filing provisional balance sheet with the competent tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification and tax classification (business registration number, corporate number, legal form, fiscal year, industry scope).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa must furnish a domestic place of business (including a fixed office for vessel hull and cargo survey work). If no permanent establishment, indicate 'no PE' and limit reporting to Korean-source income. Appoint a tax representative in Korea if required under Article 109 of the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue (총수입금액) from marine insurance surveying, inspection fees, claims assessments, and all incidental services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue sourced in Korea unless the entity has a PE. For cross-border survey work, allocate revenue using a just and reasonable basis; do not include reimbursement of expenses that represent agent payments unless separately taxable. Attach reconciliation to management accounts and e-tax invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (손금) - costs for vessel inspection, cargo damage appraisals, subcontracts, employee salary, surveys, insurance premiums, rent, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by adequate documentation and directly related to Korean-source revenue. For non-residents without PE, deductions are generally limited to direct costs traceable under the DTA. Add back non-deductible entertainment fees, fines, and excessive compensation. Use arm's length rates for subcontracted overseas survey companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income (과세표준) after applying tax adjustments, tax-exempt income, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Perform full transfer pricing documentation if cross-border related-party transactions with shipowners, reinsurance brokers, or foreign affiliated surveyors exceed the statutory threshold. Adjust intercompany fees to arm's length. For a PE-less foreign corporation, the taxable base is limited to the gross-up amount must be based on treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax and tax credits (산출세액 및 세액공제).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply progressive corporate rates (10-25%) and the 10% local surtax. Claim foreign tax credit for foreign-source income if a PE exists; claim treaty withholding credit if license fees were subject to domestic withholding. R&D credits for vessel safety algorithms or digital surveying tools may be claimed if qualified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after preliminary payments, withholding credits, and payments on behalf of foreign shareholders (납부할 세액).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities, any Korean tax withheld at source is final. If no PE, do not file a global income return; payments received for marine surveying are subject to withholding under the ITA/DTA. Attach bank evidence of prepayments. Compute late payment surcharge if any.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without justifiable cause: 20% surcharge of unpaid tax (omission surcharge); false filing: 40% surcharge of unjustified refund; overdue payment: 0.022% per day (max 10 years) plus interest; criminal penalty for fraudulent evasion: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to KRW 30-100 million (Punishment of Tax Evaders Act).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate income withholding + 2% local income surtax) on dividends paid to foreign corporations, unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty (commonly 5-15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must (1) obtain and submit an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence country; (2) submit a beneficial ownership declaration, statement of assets, and substance evidence (local employees, office, management) if required; (3) file Form 'Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax' with the NTS before payment; (4) retain supporting documents for at least 5 years. Further, the NTS may require the shareholder to prove that the entity is not a mere conduit and has the economic capability to hold shares. For dividends, if the treaty requires a minimum shareholding period (e.g., 12 months), evidence of holding must be provided.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 22% (20% + 2% local); treaty rate often 0-10%. Royalties: statutory 22%; treaty rate usually 0-15%, often 10% for industrial/technical fees. Charges for marine survey software licenses, use of patents or proprietary inspection techniques are treated as royalties and require gross-up analysis under DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: aggregate cross-border related-party transaction value ≥ KRW 10,000,000,000; Master File: consolidated group revenue ≥ KRW 1,000,000,000,000 and Korean related-party transactions ≥ KRW 5,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea does not maintain a Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style ESR regime, the substance-over-form doctrine applies under the Corporate Tax Act and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA). A Korean marine insurer surveyor must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea if it contracts with global reinsurers; otherwise the NTS may recharacterize the entity as a shell and deny treaty benefits. Actual place of effective management (APEM) is crucial for residency. Maintain local contracts, personnel, decisions, bank accounts, and claim settlement functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or under-reporting Korean-source marine survey fees and claims assessment income, or fabricating invoices/bogus expenses with related foreign adjusters to reduce taxable income in the Korean corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (조세범처벌법) Article 3 - imprisonment with labor up to 3 years, or fine up to KRW 30,000,000 (with aggravated fine up to 5 times total evaded tax if combined with false tax invoices); additional surcharge tax of 20-40% of omitted underpaid tax is assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable for the company's unpaid taxes where the veil is pierced due to fraud. They face asset seizure, overseas travel ban (출국금지), inclusion on the high-risk delinquent taxpayer list, disqualification from future board position, and criminal sentence of imprisonment up to 3 years in their personal capacity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing filing violation and arm's length breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, submit, or retain the required Local File/Master File for cross-border related-party reinsurance commissions or group service fees above the statutory threshold, or charging non-arm's length royalty/interest rates to the Korean surveyor without adequate economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) Article 11 and Enforcement Decree, non-submission of documentation may attract penalty up to KRW 50,000,000; the NTS may disregard the transaction and make upward adjustment to taxable income together with 10% additional charge on under-reported tax and daily delinquency surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false transfer pricing documentation face civil liability for restitution of the corporation's tax losses; personal liability may be imposed on the director who signed the disguised agreements. In aggravated cases, the NTS may report to the prosecution for obstruction of tax collection, leading to imprisonment up to 2 years, plus a travel ban and blacklisting of the corporate group.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / abusive treaty shopping with no economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a letterbox entity with no employees or physical presence in Korea, while the real management and decision-making are exercised overseas; using the Korean entity to access tax treaty benefits and remit profits as dividends or fees to a resident of a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS may apply the beneficial ownership test and substance-over-form doctrine to deny treaty relief under Article 14-2 LCITA; the company is re-assessed at the 22% withholding rate as dividend/royalty distribution, plus a 20% unfaithful-declaration surcharge. If foreign account reporting is breached, Real Name Financial Transaction Act may impose fines up to 80% of the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing exposes the directing minds (including foreign non-resident directors) to full personal liability for tax arrears and restitution; travel bans are imposed until taxes are settled; criminal charges of fraud under the Criminal Act (Article 347) or special tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment between 1 and 7 years.
